div.head: VI As 2
div.ab: Oðer: þæt we cwædon, þæt ure ælc scute IIII pæng̅ to ure gemæne þearfe binnan XII monðum; ⁊ forgyldon þæt yrfe, þe syððan genumen wǽre, þe we þæt feoh scuton; ⁊ hæfdon us ealle þa ǽscean gemǽne; ⁊ scute ælc man his scll', þe hæfde þæt yrfe þæt wǽre XXX pænig̅ wurð, buton earmre wúdewan, þe nænne forwyrhtan næfde ne nán lánd.

Secundum. Diximus, ut unusquisque nostrum ponat unum denarium ad nostrum commune commodum; et persoluamus pecus illud (omne pecus) quod captum fuerit (est), postquam pecuniam nostram contulerimus (-limus). Et habeamus nobis omnes eam inquisitionem communiter; et conferat omnis homo denarium suum, qui habet pecus XXX denarios ualens, exceptis pauperibus uiduis que nullum in eo forisfactum (nullam in eo culpam) habent nec terram aliquam.

Oðer: Þæt we cwædon, þæt ure ælc scute IIII pæn̅g̅ to ure gemæne þearfe binnan XII monðum; ⁊ forgyldon þæt yrfe, þe syððan genumen wǽre, þe we þæt feoh scuton; ⁊ hæfdon us ealle þa ǽscean gemǽne; ⁊ scute ælc man his scll., þe haefde þæt yrfe þæt wǽre XXX pæni̅g̅ wurð, buton earmre wúdewan, þe nænne forwyrhtan næfde ne nán lánd.

Zweitens: dass wir bestimmten, dass jeder von uns in [je] zwölf Monaten 4 Pfennig einschiesse zu unserem gemeinschaftlichen Nutzen; und dass wir das Vieh ersetzen werden, welches künftig, nachdem wir dies Geld eingeschossen haben, entwendet wird, und [dagegen] alle diese Nachforschung [Diebstahlsklage sammt Gewinn aus Verbrechergut] für uns gemeinsam erhalten; und [zwar, dass] jedermann seinen Schilling einschiesse, welcher so viel Vieh hat, welches 30 Pfennig werth ist; ausgenommen die arme Wittwe, welche keinen für sie [in Dienst] Arbeitenden und kein Land hat.

Secondly: that we determined that each of us contribute 4 pence in [every] twelve months for our common benefit; and that we will replace the cattle which is stolen in future, after we have contributed this money, and [in return] retain all this search [the theft-suit together with the profit from the criminal's goods] jointly for ourselves; and [namely, that] everyone contribute his shilling who has as much livestock as is worth 30 pence; except the poor widow who has no one working [in service] for her and no land.

Second: We have declared that each one of us shall annually contribute four pence for our common benefit; and we shall pay compensation for property which is stolen after we have made our contributions; and quests [for missing property] shall be carried out by all of us together. And everyone shall pay his shilling who has property which is worth thirty pence, except poor widows who have no land and no one to work for them.

Secondly: we pronounced that each of us was to contribute four pence for our common necessities within twelve months, and we were to compensate for the property that might be taken after we had contributed that money; and we were to have all the searching for ourselves in common. And each man was to pay his shilling who had property that was worth 30 pence, except for a poor widow, who had no one working for her and no land.

Hier beginnt ein vom Staatsgesetz unabhängiges Gildenstatut. Die redenden Wir sind zwar persönlich mit der bisher ‘wir’ heissenden Gerichtsgemeinde identisch, handeln aber hier als Gildebrüder oder zum Landfrieden Verbündete. — Mir scheint IIII richtig, und Q dies als un̄ verlesen zu haben; Q änderte gemäss dem ersten Irrtum 10 Z. weiterhin scll. zu den. [Ein Pfennig ist nämlich der Beitrag der Gilden von Abbotsbury und Woodbury für lediglich religiöse Zwecke ohne polizeilichen und Versicherungszweck.] London hatte noch ein Menschenalter zuvor unter Mercien gestanden und rechnete daher 4 Pf. = 1 Schilling (s. d. Gl 6); s. u. Erkl. 7. Nur Q führt zu 6, 2 die Westsächs. Rechnung zu 5 Pf. ein

Here begins a gild statute independent of the law of the state. The ‘we’ who speak are indeed personally identical with the court community hitherto called ‘we’, but here act as gild brethren or as men bound together for the peace of the land. — In my view IIII is correct, and Q misread it as un̄; in accordance with this first error Q altered scll. to den. 10 ll. further on. [One penny is in fact the contribution of the gilds of Abbotsbury and Woodbury for purely religious purposes, without any police or insurance purpose.] London had still been under Mercia a generation before and therefore reckoned 4 pence = 1 shilling (see that word in Gl 6); see below note 7. Only Q introduces, at 6, 2, the West Saxon reckoning of 5 pence

S. o. Erkl. 1. Die Beisteuer scheint für die, welche nur das Minimum des zu Besteuernden besassen, prozentual hoch; doch war ierfe (Vieh) nicht das ganze Vermögen, und wird wahrscheinlich die Jahresrente, nicht der Besitzstand, eingeschätzt. Die 4 Pf. dienen nicht bloss für Spurfolge (Nacheile-)Kosten. — 30 Pf. ist der Wert eines Ochsen; 3. 8, 5

See above note 1. The contribution seems high in percentage terms for those who possessed only the minimum liable to assessment; but ierfe (cattle) was not the whole of their property, and it was probably the annual income, not the property held, that was assessed. The 4 pence serve not merely for the costs of following the trail (pursuit). — 30 pence is the value of an ox; 3. 8, 5

Gildeschwestern kommen auch in anderen Genossenschaften (s. d. Gl 3g) vor, besonders Witwen (s. d. 7a) früherer Genossen. — Die Bed. des forwyrhta ist strittig. Jedenfalls irrig denkt Q an Zusammenhang mit forwyrcean ‘verwirken’. — Auch Deutsch ‘Vorwerk’ ist wohl silbenhaft verwandt, erklärt aber nicht, wie Thorpe meint, die Gesamtbedeutung; als ‘Vertreter’ (s. d. Gl 13) kann kein ‘Gutsvogt’ oder (wie an der einzigen anderen Stelle, die Wb und Toller allein anführen) Beamteter eines Höheren gedacht sein, was ja durch die ‘Armut’ schon ausgeschlossen wäre, wohl aber an einen abhängigen Landarbeiter: vielleicht ist geradezu land ⁊ forwyrhla Ein Begriff: ‘Landwirtschaft, Bodennutzung’. Nicht belegt ist die Bed. ‘Schützer, Patron’, die unser Deutsches ‘Vertreter (Gl 1)’ haben kann; sondern auch in der anderen Stelle steht der Vertreter unter dem Vertretenen

Guild sisters occur in other associations too (see that word in Gl 3g), especially widows (see that word 7a) of former members. — The meaning of forwyrhta is disputed. Q is in any case wrong to think of a connection with forwyrcean ‘forfeit’. — German ‘Vorwerk’ too is probably related in its syllables, but does not, as Thorpe thinks, explain the overall meaning; as ‘representative’ (see that word in Gl 13) one cannot think of a ‘bailiff’ or (as in the only other passage, the one which Wb and Toller alone cite) an official of a superior, which would indeed already be ruled out by the ‘poverty’, but rather of a dependent farm labourer: perhaps land ⁊ forwyrhla is actually a single concept: ‘farming, use of the land’. The meaning ‘protector, patron’, which our German ‘Vertreter (Gl 1)’ can have, is not attested; rather, in the other passage too the representative stands below the person represented
The shilling mentioned here seems to be the Mercian shilling, which contained four pence (see note 1 to Ine, cap. 59). Down to 911 London had been a Mercian town.

note.label: searching
note.seg: The quests after stolen cattle, but here more particularly the profits arising from them or from any litigation about stolen goods.
